latest_nl_proof:
Proof. If q = 0, then the sum over i is empty, so it equals 0, and also s(Lambda) = 0 by definition. Thus the claimed inequality holds.

Assume now q > 0. Fix i in {1,...,q} and let Gamma_i be obtained from Lambda by removing lambda_i.

First, Gamma_i is a numerical semigroup. Because lambda_i is an effective generator, it is a positive element of Lambda, so 0 belongs to Gamma_i. Its complement in the nonnegative integers is the complement of Lambda together with the single extra missing element lambda_i, hence is finite. For additive closure, let a and b belong to Gamma_i. Then a and b belong to Lambda, so a+b belongs to Lambda. If a+b were equal to lambda_i, then either one of a,b would be 0, forcing the other to be lambda_i and therefore not in Gamma_i, or both a and b would be positive elements of Lambda with a+b = lambda_i, contradicting that lambda_i is a minimal generator of Lambda. Hence a+b is not lambda_i, so a+b belongs to Gamma_i. Therefore Gamma_i is a numerical semigroup.

Next, F(Gamma_i) = lambda_i. Indeed, lambda_i is not in Gamma_i. On the other hand, since lambda_i is effective, lambda_i > F(Lambda). Because F(Lambda) is the largest integer not in Lambda, every integer n > F(Lambda) lies in Lambda. In particular, every n > lambda_i lies in Lambda; and since n is not lambda_i, it also lies in Gamma_i. Thus every integer larger than lambda_i belongs to Gamma_i, while lambda_i does not. So the Frobenius number of Gamma_i is exactly lambda_i.

Now consider any j > i. Then lambda_j belongs to Gamma_i, and since the list is increasing, lambda_j > lambda_i = F(Gamma_i). I claim that lambda_j is a minimal generator of Gamma_i. If not, there would exist positive a,b in Gamma_i with lambda_j = a+b. But then a,b are also positive elements of Lambda, giving a decomposition of lambda_j in Lambda, contrary to the fact that lambda_j is a minimal generator of Lambda. Hence lambda_j is an effective generator of Gamma_i. Therefore Gamma_i has at least q-i effective generators, namely lambda_{i+1},...,lambda_q.

If lambda_i is strong, then by definition m(Lambda)+lambda_i is a minimal generator of Gamma_i. Since m(Lambda) > 0, this element is larger than lambda_i = F(Gamma_i), so it is an effective generator of Gamma_i. It is distinct from all lambda_j with j > i: if m(Lambda)+lambda_i = lambda_j for some j > i, then lambda_j would be written in Lambda as the sum of the two positive elements m(Lambda) and lambda_i, contradicting the minimality of lambda_j in Lambda. So in the strong case Gamma_i has at least (q-i)+1 effective generators.

Define epsilon_i to be 1 if lambda_i is strong and 0 otherwise. The previous paragraph shows that for every i, e(Gamma_i) >= (q-i) + epsilon_i.

Summing over i = 1,...,q, we obtain sum_{i=1}^q e(Gamma_i) >= sum_{i=1}^q (q-i) + sum_{i=1}^q epsilon_i = (q-1)+(q-2)+...+1+0 + s(Lambda) = q(q-1)/2 + s(Lambda), because sum_{i=1}^q epsilon_i is exactly the number of strong effective generators. This is the required inequality.
role_in_parent: Provides the local child-sum inequality for one parent, including the q = 0 case that fixes the earlier coverage gap.
statement_nl: Let Lambda be a numerical semigroup, meaning a cofinite additive submonoid of the nonnegative integers containing 0. Let F(Lambda) be its Frobenius number, defined as the largest integer not in Lambda, with the convention F(Lambda) = -1 for the whole set of nonnegative integers. Let m(Lambda) be the least positive element of Lambda. A minimal generator of Lambda is a positive element x of Lambda that cannot be written as a+b with positive a,b in Lambda. An effective generator of Lambda is a minimal generator x with x > F(Lambda). Let q be the number of effective generators of Lambda. If q > 0, list them increasingly as lambda_1 < lambda_2 < ... < lambda_q; if q = 0, regard this as the empty list. For each i with 1 <= i <= q, define Gamma_i to be the set obtained from Lambda by removing lambda_i; if q = 0 there are no Gamma_i. Call an effective generator lambda_i strong if m(Lambda) + lambda_i is a minimal generator of Gamma_i, and let s(Lambda) be the number of strong effective generators of Lambda; when q = 0 this number is 0. For any numerical semigroup Sigma, let e(Sigma) denote the number of its effective generators, meaning the number of minimal generators y of Sigma satisfying y > F(Sigma). Then the sum over i = 1 to q of e(Gamma_i), interpreted as 0 when q = 0, is at least q(q-1)/2 + s(Lambda).

domain_restrictions: Lambda is a cofinite additive submonoid of Z_{≥ 0} containing 0 (numerical semigroup)
F(Lambda) is defined as the largest integer not in Lambda; if Lambda = Z_{≥ 0}, then F(Lambda) = -1
m(Lambda) exists as the least positive element of Lambda (implied by numerical semigroup structure; if Lambda = Z_{≥ 0} then m(Lambda)=1)
Minimal generator definition: x in Lambda is a positive element that cannot be written as a+b where a,b are positive elements of Lambda
Effective generator definition: x is a minimal generator and satisfies x > F(Lambda)
q is the number of effective generators; q can be 0, in which case (lambda_1,...,lambda_q) is the empty list
For i in 1..q, Gamma_i is the set obtained from Lambda by removing exactly lambda_i
e(Sigma) is only meaningful as stated when Sigma is a numerical semigroup; implicit in the use of e(Gamma_i) is that each Gamma_i is a numerical semigroup
Strong condition: lambda_i is 'strong' iff m(Lambda)+lambda_i is a minimal generator of Gamma_i
Arithmetic: q(q-1)/2 is interpreted in integer arithmetic consistent with q being an integer (typically the rational value which is an integer for integer q)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim:
For every numerical semigroup Lambda, let q be the number of effective generators of Lambda, enumerated increasingly as lambda_1<...<lambda_q (empty if q=0). For each i in {1,...,q}, set Gamma_i = Lambda \ {lambda_i}. Let s(Lambda) be the number of indices i in {1,...,q} such that m(Lambda)+lambda_i is a minimal generator of Gamma_i. Then, with the convention that the sum is 0 when q=0, we have

(sum_{i=1}^{q} e(Gamma_i)) >= q(q-1)/2 + s(Lambda),

where e(Sigma) is the number of effective generators of Sigma (minimal generators y of Sigma with y > F(Sigma)).
quantifier_order: forall Lambda (numerical semigroup), then define F(Lambda), m(Lambda), q, the ordered list (lambda_1,...,lambda_q) of effective generators
for each i with 1 <= i <= q, define Gamma_i by removing lambda_i from Lambda
define s(Lambda) as the count of indices i in 1..q such that lambda_i is 'strong' (m(Lambda)+lambda_i is a minimal generator of Gamma_i)
then the inequality holds: sum_{i=1 to q} e(Gamma_i) >= q(q-1)/2 + s(Lambda) (with sum interpreted as 0 if q=0)

witness_dependencies: The ordered list lambda_1 < ... < lambda_q is uniquely determined by Lambda as the increasing enumeration of effective generators of Lambda
Each Gamma_i depends on Lambda and on the corresponding effective generator lambda_i (Gamma_i = Lambda \ {lambda_i})
The strong/weak status of lambda_i depends on Lambda through both m(Lambda) and the minimal-generator structure of Gamma_i
s(Lambda) depends on the collection {Gamma_i} and on the condition 'm(Lambda)+lambda_i is a minimal generator of Gamma_i'
Each term e(Gamma_i) depends on Gamma_i, hence on Lambda and i
